verses.text: These were the groups of the gatekeepers. From the Korahites there was Meshelemiah son of Kore, one of the sons of Asaph.
Meshelemiah's sons were Zechariah the firstborn, Jediael the second, Zebadiah the third, Jathniel the fourth,
Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth, and Eliehoenai the seventh.
Obed-Edom's sons were Shemaiah the firstborn, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third, Sacar the fourth, Nethanel the fifth,
Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, and Peullethai the eighth. God had truly blessed Obed-Edom.
His son Shemaiah also had sons. They were leaders in their family, because they were very capable men.
Shemaiah's sons were Othni, Rephael, Obed, and Elzabad. Their relatives Elihu and Semachiah were also capable men.
All these were descendants of Obed-Edom. They and their sons and relatives were capable men, strong enough for the work. There were sixty-two of them from Obed-Edom.
Meshelemiah had eighteen sons and relatives who were capable men.
Hosah, one of the Merarites, had sons. Shimri was the chief. He was not the firstborn, but his father made him the chief.
Hilkiah was second, Tebaliah third, and Zechariah fourth. Hosah had thirteen sons and relatives in all.
These groups of gatekeepers, led by their chief men, had duties for serving in the LORD's temple, just as their relatives did.
They drew lots for each gate, family by family, young and old alike.
The lot for the East Gate fell to Shelemiah. Then they drew lots for his son Zechariah, a wise adviser, and the North Gate fell to him.
The South Gate fell to Obed-Edom, and the storehouse fell to his sons.
The West Gate and the Shallecheth Gate on the upper road fell to Shuppim and Hosah. The guards stood side by side.
Six Levites stood guard each day at the east, four at the north, four at the south, and two at a time at the storehouse.
At the court on the west side, there were four at the road and two at the court itself.
These were the groups of gatekeepers from the descendants of Korah and Merari.
Their fellow Levites, led by Ahijah, were in charge of the treasuries of God's temple and the treasuries of the gifts set apart for God.
The descendants of Ladan, who were Gershonites through Ladan and heads of the families of Ladan the Gershonite, included Jehieli.
Jehieli's sons, Zetham and his brother Joel, were in charge of the treasuries of the LORD's temple.
From the clans of Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel:
Shebuel, a descendant of Gershom son of Moses, was the chief officer in charge of the treasuries.
His relatives through Eliezer were Eliezer's son Rehabiah, Rehabiah's son Jeshaiah, Jeshaiah's son Joram, Joram's son Zichri, and Zichri's son Shelomoth.

Shelomoth and his relatives were in charge of all the treasuries of the gifts set apart for God. These gifts had been given by King David, by the heads of families, by the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and by the other army commanders.
They had given some of the goods taken in battle to repair the LORD's temple.

Everything that Samuel the seer, Saul son of Kish, Abner son of Ner, and Joab son of Zeruiah had set apart for God, and everything anyone else had set apart, was in the care of Shelomoth and his relatives.
From the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons were given work away from the temple. They served as officials and judges over Israel.

From the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his relatives, one thousand seven hundred capable men, were put in charge of Israel west of the Jordan River. They took care of all the LORD's work and the king's service.

From the Hebronites, Jerijah was the chief, according to the records of their families. In the fortieth year of David's rule, the records were searched, and capable warriors from this family were found at Jazer in Gilead.

Jerijah had two thousand seven hundred relatives who were capable men and heads of families. King David put them in charge of the tribes of Reuben and Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh, for everything that had to do with God and with the king.
